findings.title: MNIST presentation-time estimate needs correction or an explicit subset
findings.claim: 500ms per image and almost seven hours for one MNIST training epoch

premise_check.source: Original-format train-labels IDX gzip header; official Keras documentation

findings.counterevidence: An unstated 50,000-example training subset could explain the estimate. No such partition was found in the inspected text.
findings.impact: Bounded arithmetic/setup-description discrepancy. Corrected longer duration preserves the central practical-time argument; no material central-claim failure demonstrated.
findings.repair: Use 8h20m for 60,000 examples or state the 50,000-example subset; label presentation-only time before overhead.
findings.repair_status: Exact arithmetic verified; no training or biological experiment performed.

scope_clarifications.status: No Issue Found within inspected scope
scope_clarifications.details: Kagan includes human iPSC and primary mouse cultures; Jordan uses human iPSC-derived NSCs. Zhang/Elliott include other preparations used as instrumentation precedents.
Perfect composite-task accuracy alone does not localize computation; the paper permits reservoirs and calls for nontrivial-use objectives.
History/latent/belief state may be required; the paper suggests sequence models.
No convergence theorem supplied or refuted.
